rv.q: Is Idle Muse's The Three Musketeers entertaining? It is. Wildly so.
Jennifer Mohr (another Babe! ) was outstanding as Milady de Winter, intertwining lasciviousness with malevolence.
It is a fun wild ride and a truly impressive use of a small storefront to convey an epic plot and a story whose latest edition takes up 736 pages.
The Three Musketeers makes for a rollicking, old-fashioned adventure with a strong comedic sensibility.
The only problem is that the play is both a little long and sometimes feels laborious.
There is truly a sweetness anchored in camaraderie in the telling of this tale.
It’s a rollicking, romping, stomping swirl of fun.
The production’s standout achievement is its fight choreography.
The cast delivers on the ambition of the playwright in a full, grand adventure.

cn.t: Critics praise this swashbuckling adaptation as an ambitious, action-packed adventure that largely succeeds despite its length, with energetic performances and impressive physicality in a small space capturing Dumas' wit and spirit.
